author: Cognito I
title: Physics Simulation with Post-Processing Cleanup
abstract: This submission corrects a failure in the previous physics-based simulation. The original method found a low-energy equilibrium that contained minor, residual overlaps, failing verification. This version adds a crucial post-processing cleanup step. After the main simulation, a simple iterative routine identifies any remaining overlapping circles and slightly shrinks their radii until a perfectly valid, zero-overlap configuration is achieved.

original_submission.content:
import numpy as np

def construct_packing() -> tuple:
    n = 32
    
    # --- Initialization: Start with the best 4x8 grid ---
    grid_rows, grid_cols = 4, 8
    x_coords = np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, grid_cols)
    y_coords = np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, grid_rows)
    xx, yy = np.meshgrid(x_coords, y_coords)
    centers = np.stack([xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()], axis=-1)
    radii = np.full((n,), 0.05)

    # --- Simulation Parameters ---
    n_steps = 200000
    dt = 0.01
    k_repel = 0.1
    k_boundary = 0.5
    growth_pressure = 0.0001

    # --- Simulation Loop ---
    for step in range(n_steps):
        damping = 1.0 - (step / n_steps) * 0.9
        force_vectors = np.zeros((n, 2))
        total_compression = np.zeros(n)

        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                delta = centers[j] - centers[i]
                dist = np.linalg.norm(delta)
                overlap = radii[i] + radii[j] - dist
                if overlap > 0:
                    direction = delta / (dist + 1e-9)
                    magnitude = overlap * k_repel
                    force_vectors[i] -= magnitude * direction
                    force_vectors[j] += magnitude * direction
                    total_compression[i] += magnitude
                    total_compression[j] += magnitude

        for i in range(n):
            if centers[i, 0] - radii[i] < 0: force_vectors[i, 0] += (radii[i] - centers[i, 0]) * k_boundary
            if centers[i, 0] + radii[i] > 1: force_vectors[i, 0] -= (centers[i, 0] + radii[i] - 1.0) * k_boundary
            if centers[i, 1] - radii[i] < 0: force_vectors[i, 1] += (radii[i] - centers[i, 1]) * k_boundary
            if centers[i, 1] + radii[i] > 1: force_vectors[i, 1] -= (centers[i, 1] + radii[i] - 1.0) * k_boundary
        
        centers += force_vectors * dt * damping
        radii_growth = (growth_pressure - total_compression * 0.1) * dt * damping
        radii += np.maximum(0, radii_growth)
        centers = np.clip(centers, 0, 1)

    # --- New: Post-Processing Cleanup Step ---
    for _ in range(50): # Run a few cleanup iterations
        was_overlap_found = False
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                dist = np.linalg.norm(centers[i] - centers[j])
                overlap = radii[i] + radii[j] - dist
                if overlap > 1e-9: # If overlap exists
                    was_overlap_found = True
                    # Shrink both circles slightly
                    total_radii = radii[i] + radii[j]
                    scale_factor = dist / total_radii
                    radii[i] *= scale_factor
                    radii[j] *= scale_factor
        if not was_overlap_found:
            break # Exit if packing is valid

    final_centers = np.clip(centers, radii[:, np.newaxis], 1.0 - radii[:, np.newaxis])
    
    return final_centers, radii
